A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DenseMLLM study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite the changed title and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DenseMLLM benchmark results, ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–7, alongside qualitative results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds runtime measurements and estimates in Section 4.2 and a segmentation failure example in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The architecture, NTP-M objective, relevant negative sampling, dense prediction procedure, and four-stage training recipe are unchanged. Appendix B's new explanation of stage grouping concerns presentation relative to a technical report, not a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Training-data categories and evaluation coverage remain unchanged across segmentation, depth estimation, referring segmentation, and general vision-language tasks. The added failure example comes from the existing ADE20K coverage; the timing analysis introduces a setting rather than a new task or domain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark tables, ablations, applicability analysis, and visual-representation comparison. The added timing discussion concerns UFO and DepthLM, already included in the inference-cost comparison in Table 8.

E3.justification: v2 adds a timing analysis using variants within the authors' framework at 500×500 resolution, with cost assumptions for 100 DepthLM point queries and 10 UFO classes. This supplements v1's qualitative inference-cost comparison. Existing benchmark protocols and training settings in Appendices B and D remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 extends the efficiency analysis with runtime measurements and estimates. Appendix C adds Figure 10, an ADE20K failure case illustrating tree/sky overlap errors and aliasing. Existing component ablations, resolution and hyperparameter studies, and PCA analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for the results. The new timing figures do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. v2 newly reports approximately 1 s total runtime, less than 1 ms for logits operations, and approximately 5 ms per token. Its common-framework assumptions yield 100 s for 100 DepthLM points and 0.8 s additional cost for 10 UFO classes. Figure 10 also adds a qualitative failure result.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and their mathematical definitions and assumptions are unchanged, including the independent Bernoulli formulation and relevant-negative selection. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the claims of dense prediction without specialized decoders while preserving general vision-language capability. Both introductions condition this capability on appropriate supervision; the shorter title and revised opening do not substantively change that claim.

C2.justification: Figure 10 newly attributes overlap errors to patch-size constraints and identifies aliasing without high-resolution input and post-processing. The timing discussion also qualifies latency by resolution and post-processing costs. Existing limitations concerning long-tail data and unsupported dense prediction tasks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-repository link in the abstract and clarifies in Appendix B that some pretraining stages were consolidated for presentation relative to the technical report. Table 9's hyperparameters, the fine-tuning budget, and Appendix D's processing and prompt instructions are retained.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive research positioning remain stable. Changes to entries such as UniPixel, UFO, DINOv2, and DAPO are bibliographic updates. Section 2 corrects the VisionLLM citation to Wang et al. (2023b), a work already referenced in v1.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, some introductory wording is revised, and Appendix C is renamed from Qualitative Examples to Case Study. Conflict-of-interest and acknowledgment sections and brief explanatory passages are added. Most prose and the overall section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the full-page failure visualization in Figure 10. Existing Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–9 retain their displays, with limited caption-reference updates, placement shifts, and text reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency through a concrete failure example and explanation, supplementing v1's successful qualitative examples. The timing analysis adds numerical context to the earlier qualitative cost comparison, and project-access and provenance disclosures improve documentation. These gains are limited: the external-method timing estimates depend on common-framework assumptions and lack hardware and uncertainty details, while the core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
